page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor using the x86_64 architecture. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, alongside 32 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4 GB of RAM per vCPU. The processor includes a 32 MB L3 cache and supports hardware-level instructions such as AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA_NI for cryptographic operations. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong single-core CPU performance, placing in the top 25% of tested servers. Multi-core performance, memory bandwidth, and cryptographic execution fall within the average range. For instance, the server achieves a read-only large block memory bandwidth of 45.33 GB/sec and a write bandwidth of 26.94 GB/sec. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is a relative bottleneck, performing in the bottom 25%. However, web serving throughput and Redis SET operations remain highly consistent with standard mid-tier expectations.

Operating on AMD EPYC hardware, the n2d-standard-8 offers a balanced resource density that provides qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring dedicated CPU allocation without the overhead of specialized memory or storage arrays. It is well-suited for general-purpose applications, including static web serving, database operations, software compilation, and light text or image processing tasks.
